steps: Mix the besan, turmeric and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves.
Whisk in about 60 ml water a person, a little at a time, until the batter is smooth and pours like thick cream.
Heat a flat pan on medium heat and wipe it with a few drops of oil.
Stir the batter, pour a ladle into the middle and quickly spread it into a thin round with the back of the ladle.
Drizzle a little oil round the edge and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the base has golden spots.
Flip, press down with a spatula and cook the other side for 1 to 2 minutes, until it has light brown spots.
Repeat with the rest of the batter and serve hot with chutney or ketchup.
note: A serving is now two chillas, about 50 g of besan; the old amounts were for one. Oil is now counted at about a teaspoon per chilla, and the red chilli powder used by only one source is left out.
